{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting / Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against the playbook. The commercial architecture is, on balance, favourable to us in several important respects: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum-purchase take-or-pay of concern, no non-solicit and no audit right running against Client; the MFN runs in our favour; Client holds an unconditional termination-for-convenience right effective at the end of the following month with no exit fee; and renewal is 12 months with a mutual 30-day non-renewal window. Governing law (California, no arbitration) sits at our accepted fallback.

The risk is concentrated in the vendor-obligation provisions. Four items are critical or structural:

- **One-way limitation of liability** — TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting/support compensation while Client's liability, including under the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited. There is no mutual consequential-damages exclusion. This is walk-away territory.
- **Vendor indemnity is too narrow** — limited to TrueLink's own breach or performance failure, with no third-party IP infringement prong (and no non-infringement warranty), no breach-of-law, data-incident or gross negligence/wilful misconduct prongs.
- **Credit Data licence is over-broad** — Section 8(d) lets TrueLink distribute, license, resell and exploit data of our borrowers and loan applicants, well beyond service provision.
- **No insurance covenant at all**, for a vendor that hosts our Web Site and processes borrower credit data — walk-away territory under that rule.

Also material: no vendor performance/conformance warranty (only Y2K-readiness, with everything else disclaimed), no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion, an assignment clause with no M&A/successor carve-out or reasonableness standard, and a licence grant that does not reach our affiliates or contractors.

Redlines have been prepared for each deviation and for the two missing provisions. We have deliberately left the scope of TrueLink's own liability cap untouched and sought mutuality instead.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Cap is one-way (TrueLink capped at 12 months' hosting/support compensation; Client unlimited, including under § 12(a)); no mutual consequential-damages exclusion; no statement that Client payment obligations sit outside the cap. Walk-away territory. Redline: mirrored cap on Client + mutual consequential-damages exclusion. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Vendor indemnity covers only its own breach/performance failure; no third-party IP infringement (and no non-infringement warranty), breach of law, data incident or gross negligence prong, while Client's § 12(a) indemnity is unusually broad. Fails fallback. Redline: add the four standard prongs. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | § 8(d) grants TrueLink rights to distribute, license, resell and exploit Credit Data (borrower/applicant data) beyond service provision. Ownership elsewhere is acceptable (Interface under § 2(d); Client domains and Client Content under § 13; Client IP and service results as Client Proprietary Information under § 10). Redline: narrow the licence to service provision; confirm Client's retained rights. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 is mutual and permits affiliate transfers but has no M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent, so TrueLink could block a transfer on our merger or asset sale — short of fallback. Redline: successor carve-out on notice, "not unreasonably withheld", and no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client only; § 8(c) limits access to Client's own officers, employees and approved agents, with no path to add group companies — short of the fallback (affiliates on notice). Grant is not revocable at will and runs for the term; Exhibit A sites amendable by notice. Redline: extend to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf. |
| 6 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only express vendor warranty is Y2K-readiness (§ 9); no conformance-to-documentation warranty and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; balance disclaimed in § 12, with § 11 offering only a self-referential standard of care. Fails fallback. Redline: workmanlike + 90-day conformance warranty with remedies, carved out of the disclaimer. |
| 7 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Exit obligations run only against Client (new name server and hosting environment); TrueLink owes no transition assistance, no return or export of Client Content, Credit Data or backups, and no deletion certification. Redline: six-month transition assistance, 30-day data return, certified deletion; 90 days of assistance is our fallback. |
| 8 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and processing borrower credit data — walk-away territory under this rule. Redline: short insurance section (CGL, E&O, cyber; certificates on request); E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback. |
| 9 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; licence is non-exclusive and § 2(a) confirms Client may source similar software and services elsewhere. Nothing in §§ 2, 5 or 8 requires exclusive procurement. |
| 10 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; § 2(a) preserves our freedom to build, buy or license competing software, subject only to standard IP and confidentiality limits. Note: § 8(d) refers to a separate Non-Competition Agreement, which should be reviewed on its own terms but imposes nothing here. |
| 11 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No liquidated damages, penalty, late fee or termination charge on Client, including in § 5 and the spam provisions of § 7 (breach there gives TrueLink only technical and equitable remedies). Monthly minimums addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 12 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 14 gives Client an unconditional right to terminate on notice, effective end of the following month (~30–60 days), with no early-termination fee; TrueLink has no convenience exit (§ 13 rights are breach-triggered). Meets or betters our preferred position. No express pro-rata refund mechanic, though fees are invoiced monthly in arrears. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Client; § 6 runs the other way, giving Client documentation and dispute rights. Meets preferred position. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts sits at our accepted fallback; no arbitration. Venue is San Luis Obispo County (TrueLink's home county) rather than our preferred forum — acceptable. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour: TrueLink's hosting rates may not exceed those charged to any other customer. No obligation on Client to extend best terms. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5 imposes a monthly fee floor rather than a multi-year take-or-pay, and Client can exit at any time under § 14 with no penalty — within the fallback. Commercial note: minimum amounts remain blank, and § 6 excludes those minimums from our documentation and dispute rights. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit or no-hire binding Client; solicitation/hiring/inducement search returns only the unsolicited-e-mail provisions of § 7. §§ 8 and 10 contain nothing of the kind. Matches preferred position. |
| 18 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | 12-month renewals with a mutual 30-day non-renewal window meets our preferred position; Client can exit under § 14 in any event. Minor, not redlined: no vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal increases beyond the first-year freeze and the § 6 MFN; the cross-reference to "Section 12" in § 13 should read Section 14. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These two items are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **One-way limitation of liability (§ 12 INDEMNITY.)** — an unlimited Client exposure sitting beneath a very broad § 12(a) indemnity, against a 12-month cap for TrueLink. We require a mirrored cap on Client and a mutual consequential-damages exclusion. We are not seeking to reopen the scope of TrueLink's own cap.
2. **Absence of any insurance covenant (§ 12 INDEMNITY.)** — unacceptable for a vendor hosting our Web Site and processing borrower credit data. We require CGL, E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback.

We also regard the narrow vendor indemnity and the over-broad Credit Data licence as critical; they are not on the walk-away list, but the three critical items are interdependent and should be negotiated as a package.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the five deviations (LOL-CAP, INDEMN, IP, ASSIGN, LICENSE, WARRANTY) and the two missing provisions (TRANSITION, INSURANCE), with the fallbacks noted above available where TrueLink pushes back.
2. **Negotiate the critical package first** — mutual cap plus consequential-damages exclusion, the four indemnity prongs, and the narrowed Credit Data licence — before conceding on lower-severity items.
3. **Commercial team to close open points before signature:** populate the blank monthly minimum amounts in § 5 and address the § 6 exclusion of those minimums from our documentation and dispute rights.
4. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d); it imposes nothing in this document but must be assessed on its own terms.
5. **Housekeeping:** correct the cross-reference in § 13 from "Section 12" to Section 14. We will not press the non-material points (no renewal reminder, no renewal price-increase cap beyond the first-year freeze and MFN, no express pro-rata refund on termination for convenience, San Luis Obispo County venue).
6. **Report back** to the deal team once TrueLink responds, flagging immediately if either walk-away item is refused."}
